preamble.title: Preamble
preamble.p1: These General Terms of Use and Sale (GTUS) govern the relationship between SATCHAPRODUCTION, operator of the {{brand}} music streaming platform, and the Artists using the Platform, for making their musical works available for streaming.
preamble.p2: Use of the Platform implies full and unconditional acceptance of these terms and conditions, in accordance with the provisions of the revised Bangui Agreement of OAPI and Chadian Law No. 2003-05 of January 15, 2003, concerning the protection of copyright and related rights.

article1.title: Article 1 — Purpose
article1.p1: The purpose of these GTUS is to define the conditions under which the Platform enables Artists to distribute their musical works to the public through on-demand streaming and temporary download services.

article2.title: Article 2 — Registration and Artist Account
article2.s1: To access the distribution services, the Artist must create an account by providing accurate and complete information (identity, contact details, etc.).
article2.s2: The Artist represents and warrants that they are of legal age and have the legal capacity to enter into these terms.

article3.title: Article 3 — Submission and Availability of Works
article3.s1: The Artist grants the Platform a non-exclusive license to distribute their works within the territory of the OAPI member states, and more particularly in Chad, for the duration of their subscription or use of the Platform.
article3.s2Intro: The Artist is solely responsible for the content they upload and warrants that:
s2Items: They hold all economic rights over the uploaded works (copyright, related rights).
They have obtained all necessary authorizations from any co-authors, performers, or producers.
Their works do not infringe the rights of any third party.
article3.s3: The Artist agrees to provide complete and accurate metadata for their works.

article4.title: Article 4 — Services and Remuneration
article4.s1Intro: The Platform provides the following services:

s1Items.label: On-demand streaming (VOD):
s1Items.text: individual listening to a work by users.

s1Items.label: Temporary download:
s1Items.text: caching for offline listening (within the limits of the subscription).

article4.s2: In consideration of the license granted, the Artist receives remuneration calculated on a pro-rata basis: a percentage of the Platform's total net revenue (65%), proportional to the total number of streams of their works relative to the total number of streams recorded on the Platform.
article4.s3: Revenue is calculated and paid out periodically (each quarter), subject to reaching a minimum payment threshold.

article5.title: Article 5 — Obligations of the Platform
items: Implement the technical means necessary to ensure that works are distributed under appropriate conditions.
Provide the Artist with access to a secure area to monitor their distribution statistics.
Ensure the protection of works against unauthorized use, within the limits of available technologies.
Report to the Artist on the exploitation of their works and the revenue generated.

article6.title: Article 6 — Obligations of the Artist
items: Keep their personal information and works up to date.
Not upload counterfeit works or works that infringe the rights of others.
Not attempt to defraud the stream-counting system.
Inform their collective management organizations (CMOs) of the availability of their works on the Platform, for the collection of rights not covered by the direct license.
article6.pricingIntro: 6.1 In consideration for publishing their content on the Platform, the Artist pays an annual subscription fee, expressed in CFA francs (FCFA), which varies according to their status and the format of the content uploaded, in accordance with the following schedule:
article6.labelledTitle: a) Signed artists (managed by a production company)
article6.pricingNote: 6.2 These amounts correspond to fees for publishing and maintaining content on the Platform for a period of one (1) year, renewable. They are due independently of the remuneration provided for in Article 4.2 and are payable prior to the publication of the works concerned.

article7.title: Article 7 — Intellectual Property
article7.s1: The Platform is protected by intellectual property laws. Any unauthorized reproduction or representation is prohibited.
article7.s2: The uploaded musical works remain the exclusive property of the Artist. The Platform does not acquire any ownership rights over the works, but only a license to exploit them under the conditions defined herein.

article8.title: Article 8 — Duration and Termination
article8.s1: The Artist may terminate their account at any time, free of charge.
article8.s2: The Platform reserves the right to suspend or terminate an Artist's account in the event of a serious breach of their obligations (e.g., infringement, fraud), following formal notice that remains without effect.

article9.title: Article 9 — Protection of Personal Data
article9.p1: The Platform collects and processes Artists' personal data in accordance with applicable regulations, for the purpose of managing their account and paying out their revenue.

article10.title: Article 10 — Applicable Law and Disputes
article10.s1: These GTUS are governed by Chadian law and by the provisions of the Bangui Agreement of OAPI.
article10.s2: Any dispute relating to the interpretation or performance of these terms shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the courts of Chad.

article1.title: Why does an artist need a manager?
article1.description: Discover how a manager supports an artist's career and helps turn their talent into a true professional project.
body: Talent is essential, but it isn't always enough to build a lasting career. The manager supports the artist's decisions, organizes their schedule, seeks out opportunities, and facilitates relationships with media, producers, promoters and partners.

They also help the artist define their identity, prepare their releases and develop a coherent communication strategy. While the artist focuses on creating, the manager makes sure their career stays well organized.

A good manager doesn't decide in the artist's place. They listen, advise, and protect the artist's interests. For this collaboration to succeed, responsibilities, commissions and the length of the partnership must be clearly defined in a contract.
Choosing the right manager means choosing someone you trust, who understands your vision and can support you toward your goals.

article2.title: How do you protect your music before release?
article2.description: A few essential precautions let artists and producers protect their works before publishing them.
body: Before releasing a song, the artist must be able to prove they are its author or hold the necessary rights to exploit it.

It's important to keep the different versions of the track, the studio files, the creation dates and exchanges between collaborators. Each participant's role — author, composer, performer, beatmaker, producer or sound engineer — should be clearly specified.

When a work is created by several people, a written agreement should determine everyone's rights and shares. The artist should also avoid releasing a full version of their track on social media too early.
Protecting your music isn't just about preventing theft. It's also about properly organizing your rights so you can distribute, promote and monetize your work under good conditions.

article3.title: Protecting our culture means safeguarding our future
article3.description: Our languages, rhythms and stories form a precious memory that must be passed on to future generations.
body: Culture tells the story of who we are. It lives in our languages, our songs, our instruments, our dances, and the stories passed down by our parents.

When a piece of traditional music disappears without ever being recorded, part of our collective memory fades with it. Artists therefore play an essential role: creating, documenting and passing on our heritage with today's tools.

Digital technology lets us preserve our works and make them accessible everywhere in the world. A song released online can reconnect a young person with their origins and introduce Chad's cultural richness to new audiences.
Protecting our culture doesn't mean rejecting modernity. It means using modernity to give our heritage new life and pass it on with pride.

article4.title: Why choose AsraPa to distribute your music?
article4.description: AsraPa gives artists a space dedicated to discovering, showcasing and promoting Chadian music.
body: AsraPa is a platform designed to bring Chadian artists closer to their audience, in Chad and across the diaspora.

Choosing AsraPa means joining a space that understands our music, our realities and the diversity of our culture. Every artist can showcase their world, share their work and strengthen their relationship with their listeners.

For the public, AsraPa makes it easier to find the artists, songs and sounds that represent Chad. For creators, the platform is a new digital showcase that can support their visibility and career growth.
By choosing AsraPa, artists and listeners together help build a stronger music ecosystem. Our music deserves to be heard, valued and passed on. AsraPa gives it a space to shine.
